opportunities.author: Manisha chouhan
opportunities.topic: Measuring operational consistency behind customer experience
opportunities.sourceLocator: Inbound mention replying to the user's Adobe Summit operations comment
observedNumbers: 484 impressions on the user's parent comment
opportunities.draft: Agreed, @Manisha chouhan. The useful operating measures are the percentage of event failures absorbed without attendee impact, handoff variance, and recovery time. If those improve while satisfaction stays high, the experience is not only seamless; the operating model is resilient.

opportunities.author: Pascal BORNET
opportunities.topic: Whether AI agents belong on the organization chart
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post beginning 'Should agents appear on the org chart?'
opportunities.draft: Putting agents on the org chart helps ownership, but I would add an authority chart beside it. @Pascal BORNET, four fields should travel with every agent: named human principal, maximum delegated scope, approval threshold, and kill-switch owner. Otherwise visible accountability can still hide who spent whose authority.

opportunities.author: Cael Stewart
opportunities.topic: Why AI employees should preserve human agency
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post beginning '10-20 startups have hundreds of millions of dollars in funding'
opportunities.draft: The 10–20 funded entrants make the control boundary more important, not less. @Cael Stewart, I would measure human-agency preservation through escalation precision, unauthorized-action rate, verified completion rate, and recovery time. A winner should maximize successful execution without silently converting ambiguity into autonomy.

opportunities.author: Farrukh Ahmed Khan
opportunities.topic: Enterprise AI control-plane architecture
opportunities.sourceLocator: The AI Control Plane article
opportunities.draft: The API-gateway analogy is strong, but an agent control plane must govern intent and effect, not only traffic. @Farrukh Ahmed Khan, I would make five runtime measures non-negotiable: policy-decision latency, unauthorized-action rate, evidence completeness, postcondition-verification success, and mean recovery time.

opportunities.author: Vikram V. Koppikar
opportunities.topic: Named accountability for harmful agent actions
opportunities.sourceLocator: The AI Governance Problem Nobody Is Talking About article
opportunities.draft: Naming accountability is necessary, but the seven answers should also become machine-verifiable control data. @Vikram V. Koppikar, bind each action to its principal, policy version, scoped permission, approval evidence, outcome verifier, and recovery owner; then measure orphaned actions and exception-closure time.

opportunities.author: Anuj J.
opportunities.topic: Knowledge graphs for coding-agent context
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post beginning 'Your AI coding agent sees files. Not the system.'
opportunities.draft: @Akon Labs (YC S26), moving from 37.0% to 68.4% solved while cutting run cost 51% suggests graph context affects both quality and search efficiency. The enterprise test I would add is blast-radius precision: how many predicted dependencies were real, and how many critical callers were missed?

opportunities.author: Sanjay Kumar Ph.D., MBA
opportunities.topic: Three-tier LLM memory architecture
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post titled 'LLM Memory Architecture'
opportunities.draft: @Sanjay Kumar, the three-tier model becomes operational only when each tier has an explicit retention and deletion contract. I would track recall at k, stale-fact rate, p95 retrieval latency, privacy-deletion SLA, and the percentage of answers whose memory provenance can be reconstructed.

opportunities.author: Thomas Kurian
opportunities.topic: Gemini Enterprise billing and agent cost controls
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post introducing four AI cost-management controls
opportunities.draft: @Thomas Kurian, the 20% token-saving commitment is useful, but the stronger control is tying spend caps to outcome SLOs. Teams should see cost per verified task, fallback rate, model-route distribution, and quality-adjusted savings; otherwise auto-routing can look cheaper while shifting cost into rework.

opportunities.author: Manas Jain
opportunities.topic: Decision-first architecture for enterprise agents
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post proposing Decision → Context → Sources → Permissions → Tools → Action
opportunities.draft: @Manas Jain, Decision → Context → Sources → Permissions → Tools → Action is the right build order. I would add Verification → Recovery, then instrument p95 decision latency, approval rate, false-escalation rate, successful postcondition checks, and mean time to reverse an incorrect action.

opportunities.author: Swami Sivasubramanian
opportunities.topic: AWS acquisition of DuckLabs and DuckDB
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post welcoming DuckLabs to AWS
opportunities.draft: @Swami Sivasubramanian, DuckDB's appeal is moving analytics to the data with very little operational weight. The acquisition opportunity for AWS is measurable: query latency, cross-service data movement, price-performance, and time from local prototype to governed production should improve without weakening workload portability.

opportunities.author: Oana Labes, MBA, CPA
opportunities.topic: Incomplete financial metrics and decision quality
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post contrasting EBITDA, free cash flow, net income, book value, and gross margin
opportunities.draft: @Oana Labes, this is the same denominator problem that distorts AI ROI: an impressive numerator hides capital, operating risk, and rework. A decision-ready scorecard should pair EBITDA or FCF with ROIC, cash conversion, maintenance capex, debt-service coverage, and downside sensitivity.

opportunities.author: Jaleel Ahmed
opportunities.topic: Building the control plane before scaling agents
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post and article titled 'Before You Scale Agentic AI, Build the Control Plane'
opportunities.draft: @Jaleel Ahmed, identity, policy, observability, and lifecycle governance are necessary, but the control plane also needs an evidence contract. Every material action should emit who authorized it, which policy ran, what changed, how the outcome was verified, and whether rollback remained possible.

opportunities.author: Keyur Thakker
opportunities.topic: AI cost as an architecture and governance problem
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post consolidating six AI-cost architecture posts
opportunities.draft: @Keyur Thakker, calling AI cost an architecture problem is exactly right because token price is only one term. The operating metric should be cost per verified outcome: model plus retrieval plus tool plus human-review plus failure-recovery cost. Routing and caching should be optimized against that denominator.

opportunities.author: SustainInsight
opportunities.topic: Whether AI usage should become an ESG governance metric
opportunities.sourceLocator: Poll titled 'Should AI Usage Be a Formal ESG Governance Metric?'
opportunities.draft: @SustainInsight, AI belongs in ESG governance when the metric measures operating control rather than tool inventory. Useful disclosures could include high-impact use cases with named owners, material incidents, energy per verified workload, unresolved policy exceptions, and recovery-test coverage.

opportunities.author: Raj Kumar
opportunities.topic: Cloud readiness for production-grade agents
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post asking whether enterprise cloud is ready for agentic AI
opportunities.draft: @Raj Kumar, cloud readiness for agents should be tested as an end-to-end SLO, not a capacity checklist. Measure identity-issuance latency, cross-tool trace completeness, policy-decision latency, cost per verified action, and recovery time under a failed downstream dependency.

opportunities.author: Ankit Uniyal
opportunities.topic: AI-agent governance policy and procedures
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post describing a multi-agent policy and procedure template
opportunities.draft: @Ankit Uniyal, the 24-page policy, 11 procedures, and kill-switch drills are strongest when each maps to executable evidence. I would add three KRIs: agents with standing privilege, high-risk actions lacking postcondition verification, and overdue recovery exercises.

opportunities.author: Kundan Kumar
opportunities.topic: Point-in-time feature architecture for CRM intelligence
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post and article on CRM state transitions, telemetry, and observation grains
opportunities.draft: @Kundan Kumar, point-in-time correctness is the decisive control for CRM machine learning. Beyond preventing leakage, I would measure feature freshness, label delay, training-serving skew, lineage completeness, and the percentage of scores reproducible from immutable event history.

opportunities.author: Syai Reddy Desam
opportunities.topic: Why CRM programs fail as IT projects
opportunities.sourceLocator: Article claim that 55% of CRM projects fail
opportunities.draft: @Syai Reddy Desam, the 55% claim is a useful challenge, but the governance decision needs an observable counterfactual. I would separate platform failure from operating-model failure through adoption-to-outcome conversion, process-cycle time, data-quality defects, exception backlog, and realized value per active user.

opportunities.author: Yavor Angelov
opportunities.topic: Measuring behavior change rather than AI consumption
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post proposing AI Capability × Behaviour Change = Business Value
opportunities.draft: @Yavor Angelov, the multiplication framing is useful because it makes zero behavior change visible even when capability is high. I would instrument the 30 minutes saved through customer-facing redeployment rate, cycle-time reduction, decision quality, and value per active user; time released is capacity, not realized value.

opportunities.author: Nilesh Solanki
opportunities.topic: CRM usability and shadow workflows
opportunities.sourceLocator: Post arguing that teams reverting to Excel, WhatsApp, and email indicates CRM failure
opportunities.draft: @Nilesh Solanki, Excel, WhatsApp, and email are not merely adoption symptoms; they are telemetry about missing workflow value. I would track shadow-workflow rate, duplicate-entry time, follow-up SLA attainment, stage-aging variance, and active users completing core work without leaving the CRM.
